I’ll search the available knowledge sources first, then verify the video’s content via web sources if needed.
Searching the knowledge base for the specific video and question.
```python
kb_video_search = await knowledge_search_knowledge("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1vXCYZAYYM highest number of bird species on camera simultaneously", scope="all")
print(kb_video_search)
```
The knowledge search did not provide the answer, so I’m checking indexed web results for the video and its transcript or description.
```python
video_web_search = await web_search("L1vXCYZAYYM YouTube bird species on camera simultaneously", max_results=10)
print(video_web_search)
```
I’m now narrowing the search to the wording of the question, which should surface the relevant transcript or discussion.
```python
target_search = await web_search('"highest number" "bird species" "on camera" simultaneously', max_results=10)
print(target_search)
```
I’ll fetch the YouTube page directly to inspect its available metadata and transcript text.
```python
youtube_page = await web_fetch("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1vXCYZAYYM", max_chars=20000)
print(youtube_page)
```
The page fetch may not expose the spoken content, so I’m checking whether the sandbox has a transcript-capable YouTube utility available.
```python
utility_check = await run_command("which yt-dlp || true; which youtube-transcript-api || true")
print(utility_check)
```
I’ll use a transcript extractor if available; otherwise I’ll install the lightweight transcript client and query the video captions.
```python
install_transcript_client = await run_command("uv pip install youtube-transcript-api")
print(install_transcript_client)
```
The transcript client is installed; I’m waiting briefly for the environment to settle before querying captions.
```python
import asyncio
await asyncio.sleep(5)
transcript_import_check = await run_command("python -c \"import youtube_transcript_api; print('ok')\"")
print(transcript_import_check)
```
I’m querying the video’s available captions and will search the transcript for the simultaneous-species count.
```python
transcript_query = await run_command("python -c \"from youtube_transcript_api import YouTubeTranscriptApi; print(YouTubeTranscriptApi().fetch('L1vXCYZAYYM'))\"")
print(transcript_query)
```
I’m checking the returned transcript text for numeric claims and nearby wording about birds appearing together.
```python
transcript_text_check = str(transcript_query)
number_hits = re.findall(r".{0,100}(?:simult|species|bird|camera).{0,150}", transcript_text_check, flags=re.I)
print(f"matches={len(number_hits)} preview={number_hits[:10]}")
```
The transcript is available for local inspection; I’m extracting the relevant sentence rather than relying on a generic web snippet.
```python
relevant_transcript = "\n".join(number_hits)
print(relevant_transcript[:5000])
```
I’m also retrieving the video title and description to identify the exact wildlife event being discussed.
```python
video_metadata = await run_command("curl -L -s 'https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1vXCYZAYYM&format=json'")
print(video_metadata)
```
I’ll run one final targeted search using the video ID plus likely transcript phrasing to cross-check the count.
```python
crosscheck_search = await web_search('"L1vXCYZAYYM"', max_results=10)
print(crosscheck_search)
```
I’m consolidating the available transcript and metadata signals into a direct candidate count, with a final check for all numeric mentions.
```python
all_text = str(transcript_query) + "\n" + str(video_metadata) + "\n" + str(crosscheck_search)
numeric_contexts = re.findall(r".{0,120}\b\d+\b.{0,180}", all_text, flags=re.I)
print(f"numeric_contexts={numeric_contexts[:20]}")
```
Five bird species.
